identity.real_world_identity_notes: Reiza identifies the Renault R26 in Formula V8 Gen1. Period FIA regulations establish a seven-ratio maximum and driver-controlled clutch context; exact high-downforce telemetry and behavior were established in AMS2.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim with an integrated display, shift lights, and visible paddles.

notes: The physical clutch is required to move from rest.
All seven paddle-selected gears accepted clutchless running shifts.
Automatic downshift blip was detected around exact gear changes; an upshift throttle dip was not sufficient to establish an automatic ignition cut.
Guided exact-identity test completed in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with assists disabled/unavailable.
The guided detector observed a throttle spike on downshift. Its brief upshift throttle dip could reflect driver input, traction control, or telemetry filtering, so automatic cut remains unknown.

confidence.basis: Official period context and an exact guided test establish the modeled high-downforce controls, seven gears, start requirement, automatic blip, and wheel category; automatic cut is not established.

claims.basis: Official Reiza context and exact live telemetry establish the R26 High Downforce identity.
Period regulations bound the architecture while the exact AMS2 model directly presented and accepted seven paddle-selected gears.
Guided current-game tests and cockpit inspection directly established the listed behavior; the prior throttle-only automatic-cut inference has been retracted.

notes: The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "formula". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
driver_summary: Paddle sequential needing the clutch to pull away. It blips the downshift for you, but whether it cuts the upshift was not established by the drive, so lift as though it does not.
